answer: The fuller stretches each piece of cloth on the tenterhooks and enters its length in the tentering record against the weaver who brought it. A forge piece bought from another fuller fails the record: at the lantern of the hooks the stretch must match the fuller's own frame, and strange cloth tears at the selvedge. Forging a piece means hiring a fuller, stretching false cloth and paying 8,100, and the terrace line in the tentering record is kept by the guild, so cloth whose piece was never entered is refused.
